function: Joint subchannel and transmit-power allocation per user in multi-beam LEO downlinks to maximize the system rate under beam interference and rate demands (p. 5, 9-10)
system: Multi-beam LEO downlinks: 2-4 satellites at 500 km, 2 beams each, 3-5 users per beam, 20 GHz carrier, 20 MHz split in 4 subchannels (p. 10)
method: Dynamic hypergraph neural network: 2 hypergraph-convolution layers with GRU-updated weights per snapshot, MLP heads for power and subchannel; negative-rate loss without labels, Adam, 500 epochs (p. 9-11)
data_channel: Own simulator: free-space loss and Bessel-function beam gain, perfect CSI, random user and beam positions; 1000 training snapshots, noise -120 to -80 dBm (p. 4, 10)
test_conditions: Trained on 1000 snapshots, 2-4 satellites, 3-5 users per beam (p. 10); tested on 8 snapshots within those limits (p. 11); sweeps of users, beams, height (p. 12-13)
baselines: Learned only: GCN [14], HGNN [15], GNN-DDQN [48], and GCNRA (HGNNRA with GCN layers); no non-learned method (p. 10-11)
metrics: System transmission rate, training loss, minimum-rate demand satisfaction degree R_u/R* (p. 11-13)
complexity: Time complexity O(T L (2 n_h^2 + n_h (n_o+1) + 2 n_o (|V||E| + 1 + n_i))) (p. 10); no measured runtime
q1_support: p. 4: "is the free space loss"; the channel is free-space loss plus a Bessel-function beam gain (Eqs. 1-3) with perfect CSI (p. 10). No 3GPP TR 38.811 model, QuaDRiGa or measured data.
q2_support: p. 10: "follows a uniform distribution over the set {3,4,5}" for training users per beam; p. 11: "the number of satellites and users used in the simulation was limited to the thresholds set earlier", so the test snapshots are in-distribution; Figs. 9-12 sweep further settings but the paper never says the trained model is reused.
q3_support: p. 10: "We evaluate the proposed HGNNRA algorithm with the following benchmarks": GCN, HGNN, GNN-DDQN and GCNRA, all learned (p. 10-11). No optimization, greedy or random baseline appears in the text, Figs. 6-12 or Table III.
q4_support: p. 10: "The complexity of the proposed HGNNRA is summarized as" an order in T, L, n_h, n_o, |V|, |E| and n_i; no measured runtime is reported.
q5_support: p. 10: "The locations of the beams and the number of users within each beam are randomly generated" in the authors' own simulation; no code or data link and no public channel dataset.
notes: Published version, IEEE TWC 2026, pp. 728-742. Area 6: learned joint subchannel and power allocation for LEO downlinks, which counts as physical layer for satellite links. Tables II and III (pp. 10, 13) and Figs. 6-12 were read from page images. q3 is 0 because every compared method is learned; the phrase about conventional techniques referenced in [14] and [15] (p. 2) points to GNN works. q2 is 0 under the explicit-statement rule: Figs. 9-12 use up to 10 users per beam, up to 24 beams and orbit heights of 500-900 km, beyond the training ranges, but the paper does not say whether one trained model is reused or retrained per setting; the reviewer may check this.
